I built the dry-run retention sweeper in session-core. Nothing was compiled or run (code-first rule). The patch is at C:/dev/CoresSystem/.claude/worktrees/epic-shaw-4d613b/.plan-work/execution/patches/W3-19/EP-9-C2.patch (55905 bytes, 4 files). My worktree started at the default-branch HEAD; I detached it to model-plane 0e30f0931 before editing.

How it works:
- It lists the orgs that own personal threads here and asks org-core's C1 route POST /internal/orgs/:orgId/retention/check for each, reusing ORG_CORE_URL, SESSION_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN and the x-service-id/x-service-token headers from org_policy.rs. The first call has an empty list and reads the window, revision and org hold. After that, candidates go in pages of 500 (org-core's MaxCheckThreadIDs), one check call per page.
- No row is written when org-core answers 404 or the window is null. Any other failure ends the org's pass with error_code policy_unavailable and zero counts (fail closed). A window outside 30..3650 days gives policy_window_invalid. A revision or window that changes mid-pass gives policy_changed.
- A thread is a candidate when it has no space_id and no space_kind, has been idle past the window, and has no unfinished run (status not completed, failed or cancelled). Idle time uses the later of threads.last_activity_at and the newest updated_at/ended_at of its runs. The cutoff is read once per pass from the database clock.
- Counts: threads whose every run was 'zdr' go to skipped_zdr and are not sent to org-core. Waived threads hold content, so they are swept. Threads named in held_thread_ids, or every thread while org_held is true, go to held. The rest go to would_delete.
- For the would-delete threads it also counts rows per table in the THREAD_BOUND_TABLES list (16 tables) and stores them in rows_by_table JSONB. This list is the registered list C-B9 asks for. One test scans the migration files and one checks the real schema; each fails when a table with a thread_id column is missing from the list.
- One retention_sweep_runs row and one audit outbox row (event retention_sweep, flat audit-core shape, counts only) are written in the same transaction.
- A session advisory lock stops two replicas sweeping at the same time.
- The switch SESSION_RETENTION_SWEEP: unset, empty or off means off, and the task in main.rs then makes no database read and no org-core call. dry_run and enforce are read as written. Any other value means dry_run, never enforce. enforce runs dry in this build and the row records mode dry_run. SESSION_RETENTION_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS defaults to 21600 with a floor of 300. A pass runs at start, then once per interval.

Tests:
- Unit: switch parser, interval, window bounds, strict check parsing, page split, audit body, migration-scan table coverage, and a wiremock client test (headers, path, body, 404 means no policy, 503 is an error).
- Real-Postgres #[ignore] tests: window boundary, a recent run keeps an old thread, held thread and org hold kept, Space thread kept and ZDR thread skipped, org-core unreachable means no candidates, no window or unknown org writes nothing, the counts row and audit row are written with nothing deleted, and the registered list matches information_schema.

Changes from the design: migration 0095 is free on model-plane (round B reservation). The table has two columns the design did not list, skipped_zdr and rows_by_table; window_days and created_at were also added. Orgs are listed from the local threads table instead of an org-core /internal/orgs list, because org-core has no such list route and the check route already answers per org.

The patch is at C:/dev/CoresSystem/.claude/worktrees/epic-shaw-4d613b/.plan-work/execution/patches/W3-19/EP-9-C4.patch (43 KB). I detached the worktree to model-plane 0e30f0931 before editing. All files are LF and I kept them LF.

What the slice does, behind the switch ERASURE_HOLD_CHECK (only the literal "true" turns it on; off, nothing is asked and behaviour is unchanged):

- **session-core gdpr.rs**: new hold gate with three states (Off, Unconfigured, On). When on, it asks org-core with POST /internal/orgs/{org}/retention/check, sending up to 500 thread ids per call, and reuses the existing ORG_CORE_URL and SESSION_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN.
  - A held org or thread is refused with FailedPrecondition and the trailer x-mp-error-code=erasure_blocked_legal_hold.
  - An outage, a non-404 error status, a body that does not parse, or missing credentials is refused with Unavailable and erasure_hold_check_unavailable. The message never carries the internal cause.
  - org-core's 404 lets the erasure through: the org is not live, and its holds were deleted with it.
  - The refusal message names what stays, from HELD_THREAD_CONTENT, which includes thread_goals and artifact_revisions (C-B9).
  - purge_organization_data asks the gate before it opens its transaction.
- **session-core grpc.rs**: delete_thread checks after the owner check and before the transaction. delete_threads checks inside the transaction, after its FOR UPDATE, and refuses the whole bulk delete if the org or any thread is held.
- **org-core gdpr_handlers.go**: both hard delete and soft delete are refused with 409 erasure_blocked_legal_hold while any org or thread hold is active. If holds cannot be read, the answer is 503 erasure_hold_check_unavailable. The switch is read per request; refusals are logged with the actor.
- **BFF privacy.rs**: erase maps the two upstream codes to typed 409 and 503 envelopes built from fixed words. Every other answer passes through unchanged.
- **errors.ts**: copy added for both codes.

Tests:
- **gdpr.rs (wiremock)**: strict switch parsing; Off makes no network call; Unconfigured refuses; thread hold and org hold each refuse until released; failures refuse while a 404 does not; large deletes are paged; the C-B9 tables stay named and deleted; the purge checks holds before its transaction.
- **gdpr_hold_test.go**: switch strictness; refused while held, allowed after release; a thread hold blocks org erasure; unreadable holds give a retryable refusal; the real routes refuse before HardDelete.
- **privacy.rs**: the three mapping tests.

depth_findings.text: The org-core cron purge of a soft-deleted org (PurgeDeletedOrganizations) does not check holds, and session-core's org_held check cannot catch it: the retention check route answers 404 for a non-live org, and gdpr_hard_delete cascades the holds away before the fan-out, so a hold placed during the 30-day grace window does not stop the automatic purge.

Refused erasures are only logged (org-core log.Printf, session-core tracing). No durable audit row is written, so D-C1's 'the attempt is audited' needs an audit-outbox event (org_retention_audit_outbox or session_audit_outbox) before switch-on.

model-gateway's session_thread_error maps every FailedPrecondition to thread_persistence_not_permitted, so until the http_routes.rs shared edit lands the SPA shows the wrong refusal for a held thread delete.

delete_thread checks holds before its transaction, so a hold placed in the milliseconds between the check and the commit is not honoured; delete_threads checks under its FOR UPDATE locks, but org-core hold placement is not serialised against either.

The BFF privacy erase mapping cannot be reached today: user-core's per-user erasure does not consult holds and does not delete Model Plane conversations, so only the unit test exercises it until user-core forwards the codes.

A thread hold blocks the whole org erasure, and any held thread refuses the whole bulk delete of a user's history (all-or-nothing), not just the held threads; the refusal returns counts, not thread ids.

Live proof still to run with both switches on: place a thread hold, delete it from the SPA and see erasure_blocked_legal_hold, release, delete succeeds; place an org hold, org hard and soft delete both give 409; stop org-core, delete gives a 503 retryable refusal.

**Contract.** authored-behaviour-lint.json holds 13 closed rules: code, field, severity and limit. Lengths count Unicode characters, not bytes. It also holds the mode, the refusal shape and the transcript and tool-name rules. The .sha256 pin uses the `<hash>  <name>` form over LF text. The golden file has 28 input cases with the codes each must produce.

**Rust and Go.** mp-contracts skill_lint (std-only, plus test-only reads of the three files) and capability-core internal/skilllint implement the same rules. Both have tests that check the pin, check the rules against the contract in order, and run the golden cases.

**session-core.** `upsert_agent_skill` runs the lint after `gate_skill` and before the INSERT. Under enforce it returns `skip_reason` `skill_lint:<first error code>`. Under report it only counts `skill_lint_findings_total{code,severity,mode}`.

**D2-509 fix (no switch).** A human write (`origin = "user"`) from a caller without a verified user id now gets `skip_reason` `origin_requires_person`. The old fallback that took the owner from the request for service callers is gone. The learning sink sends `background_review` and is not affected.

**capability-core.**
- `SkillsHandler` and `SkillBundlesHandler` read `SKILL_LINT_MODE` when they are built. Only the exact words `report` and `enforce` turn it on.
- POST lints the request body.
- PATCH lints the stored row with the edit applied, inside the transaction after the owner check. It runs only for a description or content edit, or for switching a skill on. A sharing change or a switch-off is not linted.
- Under enforce, a refused write gets 422 `{error:{code:"skill_lint_failed",message,details:{findings:[{code,field,severity}]}}}`.
- A write that goes ahead adds `warnings` to its 2xx body only when there are findings.
- Bundle PUT applies only the front-matter name rule, comparing against the skill's stored name.
- With the lint off, nothing extra is read and every body is byte-identical to before. The bundle summary's `warnings` is `omitempty`.
- `skillbundle.FrontMatterName` reuses the front-matter reader that `Parse` already uses.

**Frontend.** skill-lint.ts reads findings from the 422 error and from the 2xx `warnings`, and gives each code a Norwegian and English message. SaveAsSkillDialog and SkillsSection show errors next to the field they are about. A save with warnings shows a soft note; the dialog stays open with a Done button.

**Tests written.**

- Go: `TestLintGoldenParity` and the contract/pin tests, `TestPostLintEnforce422`, `TestPostLintReportWritesAndAddsWarnings`, `TestSkillWritesAreUnchangedWhileLintIsOff`, `TestPatchLintsReenableOfLearnedText`, `TestBundleFrontmatterMismatch`, and `FrontMatterName` tests.
- Vitest: skill-lint.test.ts and two new dialog tests.

No proto change, no migration and no ZDR matrix row: the findings carry no content.
